 RAHUL CHANDRAKANT SHAH  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
 =======================================================
 Appearance:
 MS PRAGNA P JOSHI(12385) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MS SHRUTI PATHAK APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  MR HIMANSHU DESAI for the Respondent No.2  =======================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DIVYESH A. JOSHI  Date : 07/03/2025  ORAL ORDER 1. With the consent of learned advocates appearing for the parties, present application is taken up for final disposal today.
2. Rule. Learned advocates for the parties waive service of notice of Rule.

3. By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, the 'Code'), the applicant prays for quashing and setting aside the FIR being C.R.
No.11196038200072/2020 registered with Varasiya Police Station, Vadodara City for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1815/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/03/2025 undefined

4. Heard learned advocate, Ms. Pragna Joshi for the applicant, learned APP Ms. Shruti Pathak for respondent no.1 and learned advocate, Mr. Himanshu Desai for respondent no.2, who is permitted Rahul Chandrakant Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63126145/

sentences.text: I have also heard the respondent no.2 - complainant, who is present before this Court.
Learned advocate, Mr. Desai identifies respondent no.2 and confirms correctness and genuineness of the affidavit filed by him.

5. When the matter is called out, learned advocates appearing for the parties have submitted that now the dispute is amicably settled between the parties and, therefore, the respondent no.2 has filed an affidavit before this Court, copy of which is placed on record.

Upon making inquiry, the respondent no.2, who is present before this Court, has stated that he has settled the dispute with the present applicant and, therefore, if the impugned FIR is quashed, he has no objection.

6. Therefore since now, the dispute with reference to the impugned FIR is settled and resolved by and between parties, which is confirmed by the original complainant through her learned advocate,
the trial would be futile and any further continuation of proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
Therefore, the impugned FIR is required to be quashed and set aside.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/1815/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/03/2025 undefined 7.
Resultantly, this application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being C.R. No.11196038200072/2020 registered with Varasiya Police Station, Vadodara City and all other consequential proceedings arising out of said FIR are hereby quashed and set aside qua the applicant.
8. Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(DIVYESH A. JOSHI, J.) Gautam Rahul Chandrakant Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63126145/
